images.title: √250 lies between 15 and 16
images.purpose: Shows √250 on a number line between 15 and 16, closer to 16, because 15² = 225 and 16² = 256.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One horizontal number line segment across the middle with a flag and two squarings beneath.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal number line with exactly 2 labelled ticks, 15 at the left and 16 at the right, far apart. The segment between them is shaded light teal (#0072B2). A reddish purple (#CC79A7) flag stands on the line about four fifths of the way from 15 to 16, labelled √250. Under the 15 tick: 15² = 225. Under the 16 tick: 16² = 256. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: If a² < N < (a + 1)², then √N lies between a and a + 1.
images.description: Shows √250 on a number line between 15 and 16, closer to 16, because 15² = 225 and 16² = 256.

image_decisions.why: A trapped flag between two squared bounds makes a non whole root easy to place.
